messages:
maya: Quick one — customer reporting intermittent 401s and asks what to send so we can correlate. They aren't super technical. Can someone paste a short checklist we can DM them? :pray:

devx-bot: Auto-reply: See minimal repro collection steps below. If you need a template, ask.

oleg: TL;DR for non-technical users — ask for: 1) a screenshot of the Console Network request (Headers tab) showing the response + request headers, 2) the exact timestamp (date + time + timezone) when the error happened, 3) the Request/Trace ID if present, 4) the endpoint they called and a short description of what they were trying to do.

maya: can you paste short copy we can DM that customer?

oleg: Sure — copy this and tweak: "Hey — to help us tie your error to logs, could you please: (a) open the browser devtools > Network, find the failed request to api.redwood.com, take a screenshot of the request/response headers, (b) tell us the date/time you saw it, and (c) if you see a header named X-Request-Id or X-Trace-Id in that request, please copy that value and paste it here. If you used our SDK, try adding this small snippet to print the request id: `console.log('reqid', response.headers.get('x-request-id'))`. If you can also paste the exact request payload (copy the JSON from the request body) that would be great. Thanks!"

sam: Add optional advanced asks for technical users: a HAR export, curl reproduction, and service region.

oleg: For engineers, include this curl template (replace <KEY> and <REQBODY>):
```bash
curl -i \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '<REQBODY>' \n  "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate"
```
Tell them to run that from a terminal and paste the full output. The response headers will include `x-request-id` when available.

maya: Where do we find the Request ID in our Console UI if they are using the hosted dashboard?

oleg: In Console: open the Request Log -> click the failed entry -> you will see a header panel on the right with "Request ID" (UUID-like) and a debug token link. If they can't access Console, the SDKs/agent proxies will usually echo `x-request-id` in the response headers.

sam: If they say they used a proxy or mobile app and can't get headers: ask for a short video or screenshots of the sequence, timezone, and the app version. Also ask for the SDK name + version (e.g., js@2.4.1 or ios@1.0.3).

oleg: If they can grab a debug token, that's ideal — instruct them: Console > Request Log > failed request > "Create debug bundle" (or click the debug token link) and paste the token here. That token lets us pull complete traces and logs.

maya: Short checklist to DM please (single message):
oleg: "Please send: 1) Screenshot of the failing Network request (headers + response), 2) Exact timestamp (include timezone), 3) Any Request/Trace ID (x-request-id / x-trace-id), 4) Endpoint & payload you called, 5) SDK + version or platform, 6) HAR or curl output if possible, 7) Debug token from Console if you can create one. If you're non-technical, just send the screenshot + time and we'll take it from there. :heart:"

devx-bot: Tip: if you need a one-click template for non-technical customers, use: "Open browser devtools -> Network -> reproduce the error -> right click request -> Save as HAR with content -> attach here."

maya: perfect — I'm sending this now. Will follow up if they provide a token. Thanks all :thumbsup:
